description: Scores the ROUTING slice of the same merged gate prompt that target #2 (council) evaluates. There is no separate router prompt — docs/ARCHITECTURE.html's own repo layout shows gate.py as 'Council + Router, merged single call' (the §11 latency fix). This target exists because it isolates a different failure mode than target #2: every case here is constructed to be a valid, single-intent, well-scoped query, so gate_verdict and decomposition are expected to be trivially correct, and the dataset instead stress-tests genuinely ambiguous vector/graph/hybrid boundary decisions that target #2's dataset does not cover. Because both targets grade council.txt, an optimize run against EITHER dataset must be re-evaluated against the OTHER before being considered done — improving routing accuracy here could regress council's gate or decomposition behavior, and vice versa. See docs/QUERY_DECOMPOSITION.md risk 5, which documents this coupling for decomposition and now extends to routing.
note_on_scoring: Three critical criteria, so as with council.json the weighted mean cannot mirror the gate on its own (see gate_verdict_accepts and no_spurious_split below, whose weights alone would not breach the threshold). The severity gate is the operative verdict; the mean is diagnostic only.

criteria.name: route_correctness
criteria.description: The top-level route must match the expected route. vector is for questions answerable from what the code conceptually does or why it was built that way. graph is for questions with an explicit or implied structural relationship — calls, imports, defines, blast radius, circular dependencies, set intersections over dependencies. hybrid is for questions that need both: a target must first be understood conceptually and then traced structurally, or a structural fact must be explained in the context of what it means. Many cases in this set are deliberately ambiguous — a phrase like 'who else uses X' is graph despite sounding like a search, while 'find code similar to X' is vector despite sounding structural, because similarity of behavior is not an import or identifier edge. Judge only the route field. Score 1.0 on an exact match; score 0.0 otherwise.

criteria.name: gate_verdict_accepts
criteria.description: Every case in this dataset was deliberately constructed to be a clear, answerable, appropriately scoped question about a source-code repository. The output must therefore accept the query: clarity, scope, answerability and specificity should all be true. A rejection here is not a routing error but a regression in the gate's acceptance behavior, which this criterion exists to catch independently of route_correctness. Score 1.0 if all four boolean properties are true; score 0.0 if any is false.

criteria.name: no_spurious_split
criteria.description: Several cases in this dataset contain the word 'and' while still being ONE question that needs a combined answer, not two separate questions — for example asking to trace a flow AND explain each layer is a single hybrid information need, not two. The output must NOT split these into multiple sub_queries. This criterion exists to catch a specific regression: a decomposition prompt tuned to be more willing to split (from optimizing against target #2's split_* cases) could start over-splitting queries here that merely contain a conjunction without containing two distinct questions. Score 1.0 when sub_queries contains exactly one entry; score 0.0 if it contains more than one.

criteria.name: format_compliance
criteria.description: The output must contain a parseable JSON object with the four boolean gate properties, a route field, and a sub_queries list whose entries each carry a text string and a route string. A markdown code fence around the JSON counts as compliant. Score 1.0 when the JSON parses and all required fields are present with the right type; score 0.0 otherwise.
